chapter: Teenage bands and Florida road tours
title: His mother taking his earnings
summary: His mother kept every nickel he made and spent it on bills and numbers while the other boys bought clothes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So after that, I learned later on in life why these things happened to me, but you know, I was, like, I was sort of raised like a little girl in a way, because my mother never allowed me to -- like when I went out and worked, I couldn't spend any of my money like the other boys was able to, like George Kelly and those were able to get up the next morning and go and buy a pair of shoes or what not. During those days, you could put down, like a dollar on a suit and then pay $5 the next week, or something like that.

Well, me, I wasn't able to do anything like that; my mother took every nickel that I made, because I had to take care of her and my brother. See, and that's why I said earlier that I became a meal ticket, you know?

So, anyway, when all of the other boys was able to have, like four and five suits of clothes, I had a suit, period, that I wore to church. And the rest of that money, my mother took it, and paid her bills with it and played the numbers, which I detest -- to this day, I don't play numbers to this day, because of that. And my mother would spend up all my money playing numbers.
